3_reorgs.fix: watch reads only up to the block the node calls finalized (feed.finalized, feed.py:46-52; watch feed.py:90): Polygon milestone finality, irreversible by consensus, so no stored fill can be orphaned. Removed logs are journaled. The lag guard (point 1) covers a node behind the others
3_reorgs.latency_cost: finalized was 1 to 3 blocks behind latest on drpc, publicnode and tenderly in probe_endpoints (6 rounds), and 1 to 4 (median 3) in reorg_probe (107 reads on drpc); the old depth was 3, so the median lateness is unchanged and a pass can wait one block more; 1rpc serves a finalized block about 1,950 blocks old, which only stalls a pass that falls back to it

7_alert_before_public_broadcast.reading: against the plain listing (CloudFront hits on almost every poll) the engine is always first, by minutes; against the origin (cache-busted) the API shows a large fill a median 3.1 s after its block, while the engine waits for finality (1 to 4 blocks) and its next pass: with the deployed 8 s interval it is first on about 1 fill in 20, with 2 s on about 1 in 4. Reading unfinalized blocks would gain about 3 blocks at the cost of the reorg safety of point 3; not done
7_alert_before_public_broadcast.limits: one window of 15 minutes on one evening (UTC 18:31-18:46); large fills only (1,000 USD and more); 2 alerts in total (one per engine, the same trade), so the alert race has a denominator of 1; the cache-busting parameter defeats a cache the operator set and is what the fastest public reader could do, not what a plain bot sees
7_alert_before_public_broadcast.structural: an alert cannot precede the data API: evaluate() raises NotReady until the wallet's v2/activity shows the entry (enrich.py:194-196); the activity listing is cached 15 s only (measured header), so a retry 60 s later reads fresh data
